summary:
The RULE is sound and I would keep it unchanged. I checked every part of it against Isabelle's own sources and found no attack on it: ① before ③ is enforced by the shape of the function (class_param_of is the guard clause, ② is computed in its else, semantic_digest.ML:387-396); "replace, not add" is right because partial_function is the only family with both a body-carrying Defs axiom and equational rules, and it is not in the function package's registry (add_function_data has exactly two writers in the whole distribution AND the whole shipped AFP: function.ML:136 and :216); and the two "cleaner shapes" the brief invites are dead ends — the registry answer carries NO theory attribution of its own (Morphism.fact -> Thm.join_transfer re-stamps every returned theorem with the env's theory, morphism.ML:149/:219, thm.ML:674, :520), which is a positive DEFENCE of user decision F4, and f_graph/f_rel are Proof_Context.concealed (function_core.ML:449-453) so Infra_Filter rejects them outright and no treatment of them can gain anything.

The PLAN DOCUMENT is not ready to hand to an implementer. The single biggest problem is evidential, and no round-one finding stated it whole: every structural and quantitative measurement in VERIFICATION.md was taken on Spec_Rules, and the approved source (F3) is Function_Common's registry. The two are NOT interchangeable, because the function package installs its registry entry with pervasive = false (function.ML:135-136, :215-216) while Spec_Rules.add on the very next line uses pervasive = true (spec_rules.ML:165). Consequences I verified: the 40/34/20 census OVER-counts (Bit_Operations.fold2_bit_int.F is a `function` inside `locale fold2_bit_int`, Bit_Operations.thy:1747/:1754, whose only interpretations come 70 lines later at :1830-1836, so nothing keyed on the bare constant ever reaches the background theory), and it is structurally BLIND to `function` without `termination` (Spec_Rules.add sits inside the termination afterqed), which is exactly the population the psimps half of F3 exists to serve. So PLAN.md §2's numbers are numbers about something else and must be re-taken on the chosen source.

Four further things must be corrected, all in the document, none touching ①-⑤ or F1-F7: (a) the §5 test subject `instantiation … :: plus` cannot discriminate anything — I confirmed Groups.thy contains ZERO instantiation/overloading blocks, so ② is empty for Groups.plus_class.plus in every env and ③ can never fire for it whatever the branch order; shipping it violates the suite's own rule (b); (b) the §5 assertion "mentions sens_pfun_dom" can never pass — the psimps premise is built in ML as Const("Wellfounded.accp") $ R $ lhs (function_core.ML:575-576, function_common.ML:130-132) and `<f>_dom` is only a Local_Theory.abbrev created afterwards (function_core.ML:890-893), folded back by the printer; (c) §6's reason for deferring "sort after normalize" is a non sequitur — Term_Ord.term_ord settles a tie by the schematic variable's index and then NAME (term_ord.ML:127, :157-158), which is precisely what normalize erases, and I walked the two-clause example `h x True = x | h y False = y` by hand: args_ord reaches the ?x/?y pair BEFORE the True/False pair, so a pattern-variable rename reverses the sorted props; (d) the "one-time cost" of 20 constants is not a cost at all — digest and deps are computed only for WIP theories (semantic_store.ML:1795-1808) and all 20 sit in loaded HOL theories.

One item must go back to the user (F6 was decided on the false sentence in (c)), and one genuine elegance improvement is worth putting to them as a proposal rather than smuggling in: rule ③'s only guard is the proxy "② non-empty", while the thing it consumes comes from a lookup with no filter at all (Net encodes Const(c,_) as AtomK c with the type discarded, net.ML:53-62), so PLAN.md:88-89's type argument is decorative. The mixed same-theory `overloading` family that this exposes is NOT hypothetical — I read it in the AFP this repository ships: Amortized_Complexity/Pairing_Heap_List2_Analysis.thy:22-38 declares `consts sz` and, in one overloading block in that same theory, defines it by one `fun` and two `definition`s; ③ as written would drop both definition bodies from sz's digest permanently. Isabelle already spells the guard that fixes it (Theory.check_overloading, theory.ML:301-315), and together with Defs.disjoint_specs (defs.ML:162-168, which forbids a second specification with overlapping argument types) it upgrades the guard from a heuristic to a theorem. It needs one REPL probe on an ordinary polymorphic `fun` before adoption, so it is a proposal, not a defect fix.

Rejected outright: the `input_eqns` proposal (refuted twice and again by me — its heads are Frees by construction, since the package's own split_def/fname_of do dest_Free on them, and normalize erases Frees while deps_of_term collects only Consts, so a mutual block would lose the very f->g edge PLAN.md:92-94 counts on); the count guard `length infos = length from_defs` (compares two lists that stand in no relation, and is unsound in both directions); `Binding.name_of (#defname info)` as the prop name (unqualified and morphism-dependent, inconsistent with the other two branches); and the proposal to hoist the new test subjects above Test_Sensitivity.thy:19 (it would silently change the input of seven live assertions).

rulings.title: "Replace" silently drops the sibling definitions of a same-theory `overloading` family
rulings.severity: moderate (not major: zero instances in this heap; one real instance in the shipped AFP)
rulings.reason: Mechanism confirmed by me end to end. Overloading.define_overloaded returns `pair (Const (c, U), def)` with U the INSTANCE type (overloading.ML:154-161); the overloading target uses theory_declaration so the flag is dropped and the registration does reach the background theory; Item_Net.retrieve is order_list o Net.unify_term (item_net.ML:46) and Net encodes Const(c,_) as AtomK c with the type discarded (net.ML:53-62); and both same-theory Defs axioms survive same_theory (semantic_digest.ML:307-313). The scenario is NOT constructed: I read afp-2026-05-13/thys/Amortized_Complexity/Pairing_Heap_List2_Analysis.thy:22-38 myself — `consts sz :: "'a => nat"` with one overloading block defining it by `fun size_hps` and by two `definition`s, all in the declaring theory. Under ③ the two definition bodies leave sz's digest permanently: a new blind spot of exactly the class this project exists to remove. Both proposed fixes from round one are refuted: the count guard (compares the registry-info count with the Defs count, two unrelated lists; over-blocks the all-`fun` family of Doc/Isar_Ref/Spec.thy:1076-1090 and under-blocks a downstream `fun` overloading at 1=1) and `import_function_data` (get_first, so the digest would depend on Item_Net order). Routed to the user because the honest choice is between recording the shape in §6 and narrowing the approved rule ③, and the latter changes behaviour the user signed off on.
rulings.fix: Put the choice to the user (see proposals). If the guard is adopted, spell it as Isabelle does: for each retrieved info, keep it only if some `Const (c, T_reg)` in its `fs` satisfies `Sign.typ_instance thy (Consts.the_constraint (Sign.consts_of thy) c, Logic.varifyT_global T_reg)` — ONE direction, as in Theory.check_overloading (theory.ML:301-315) — and fall through to ④ when none survives; do NOT use typ_instance both ways (type.ML:446-462 checks of_sort, and the class-operation family declares with strip_sortsT then adds a sorted constraint, class.ML:402-407, so the extra direction can reject a legitimate registration). Measure one ordinary polymorphic `fun` and `Bit_Operations.linordered_euclidean_semiring_bit_operations_class.or_num` in the same REPL run before relying on it. If the guard is NOT adopted, add one line to PLAN.md §6 naming the shape (a `consts` constant with a same-theory overloading family mixing `fun` with a non-`fun` definition loses the non-`fun` bodies) and drop PLAN.md:47-50's reliance on where the `consts` declaration happens to sit — that protection is a property of probe P6's construction, not of `overloading`.

rulings.title: §6's reason for deferring "sort after normalize" is factually wrong
rulings.reason: I verified the mechanism and walked the example by hand rather than taking it on trust. term_ord.ML:127 `indexname_ord = int_ord o apply2 #2 ||| string_ord o apply2 #1`, reached through hd_ord at :157-158; for `h ?x True = ?x` vs `h ?y False = ?y` the sizes are equal, the Trueprop/eq/h heads all tie, and args_ord recurses into the function part first, so it reaches the ?x/?y pair BEFORE the True/False pair and decides by string_ord("x","y"). Alpha-variance is nowhere in that condition, so PLAN.md:135-137's stated reason is a non sequitur, and the plan's own probe P5 already exhibits two non-alpha-variant props whose order flips on a rename. The escalation claim is also right: today the raw-term tiebreak runs only inside the axiomatization fallback (semantic_digest.ML:383-384) because the Defs branch sorts by axiom name alone (:396), and PLAN.md:95-98 gives every prop of the new branch the SAME name, so this becomes the sole ordering for every multi-clause `fun`. I cut the finding's blast-radius claim: an UNCHANGED verdict walls the dependents, so the price of a flip is one re-interpretation plus one judge call, not a cascade — and 0 of the 40 function-package constants in this heap are exposed. But F6 was decided on a false sentence, and a settled decision taken on a false premise is not settled.
rulings.fix: Two edits, then the re-put. (1) PLAN.md:135-137: replace "Unreachable from one `fun` (two clauses of one `fun` cannot be alpha-variants of each other)" with the true condition — Term_Ord.term_ord settles a tie by the schematic variable's index and then name (term_ord.ML:127, :157-158) whenever the first separating position of two props is a Var/Var pair, exactly the two fields normalize erases (semantic_digest.ML:158-162); reachable from one two-clause `fun` (`h x True = x | h y False = y`), unobserved in this heap (0 of 40), cost one re-interpretation plus one judge call, dependents walled by an UNCHANGED verdict. (2) PLAN.md:97-98: drop "like the fallback" — every prop carries the same fabricated name, so the name component is dead weight and the raw-term ord is the sole order. Then hand F6 back to the user with the corrected fact. If they relax it, the code change belongs in the NEW branch only and must order by a normalised KEY, not replace the returned props: `sort (fn ((_, s), (_, t)) => Term_Ord.term_ord (apply2 normalize (s, t)))` — the props are the exported surface the sensitivity suite asserts on (semantic_digest.ML:63-65).

rulings.title: The measured "one-time cost" cannot be paid: persistent theories carry no digest
rulings.reason: Confirmed by reading the code myself: semantic_store.ML:1795-1803 states outright that the incremental fields are "Computed ONLY for WIP theories", :1804 sets `wip = not (Theory_Hash.is_persistent (Theory_Hash.hash_of thy))`, and :1806-1808 hands every entry of a persistent theory NONE/[] WITHOUT calling Semantic_Digest.semantics_of at all — which has exactly two production call sites, both inside the wip branch. So for the 20 constants of PLAN.md:55-61, all in loaded HOL theories, the ML change is unreachable and the price of the digest move is zero. "Holds a store record" is not the criterion; "holds a WIP-keyed record" is. Two corrections to the finding's own wording, neither of which reduces it: the 40/34/20 figures are correct as a census of digests that would move — what is false is the label "one-time cost"; and the §7 item-3 permission must be KEPT, because the Sim_Measure_A1 dry run needs the store copy and Sim_Measure_A1 is in no session ROOT, hence WIP-keyed, hence a real payer. Only the cost-count clause is mis-aimed. The finding's "drop the permission" disjunct would kill the plan's only end-to-end acceptance check and is rejected.
rulings.fix: (1) PLAN.md §2 last bullet (:55-61): retitle from "One-time cost in the Semantic_Embedding heap" to what it measures ("Digests that move in the Semantic_Embedding heap"), keep the figures, and add the criterion that decides who pays — only a constant in a WIP-keyed theory carries a semantic digest at all (semantic_store.ML:1804-1808; semantics.py:308-312), so all 40, being in loaded HOL theories, pay nothing. (2) PLAN.md §7 item 3 (:155-159): keep the store-copy permission; change only the second clause from "the count of record-holding function-package constants in the store (the one-time cost)" to "the count of function-package constants holding a WIP-keyed record (whose semantic_digest is non-NULL)" — the only population that can pay. Also note that a FRESH production copy may not contain Sim_Measure_A1 records at all (acceptance_step10/REPORT.md:10 says nothing touched the production store), in which case `narquil` would count as a seed merely by being uncached, proving nothing.

rulings.title: A pre-gate WIP record is forced CHANGED, mints, and enrols its dependents
rulings.reason: The mechanism is exactly as quoted (semantic_interpretation.py:1443-1445 sets CHANGED with no prefilter and no judge when the stored baseline is None; CHANGED mints and _propagate enrols theory-internal dependents), and both defenders agree it survives. But three of the four framings do not. It is not a defect of THIS plan: forced CHANGED on a baseline-less record is a settled decision already booked as an accepted one-time cost in SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:140/:146-148. It cannot touch the population PLAN.md §2 counts, for the reason established in invalidation-1. The trigger is narrower than "written before 2026-09-12" — a record with no digest at all takes gate §3 row 1, which does not mint. And the closure is not "every theorem mentioning it, each minting in turn": theorem-alike dependents are never judged and never mint, so the recursion runs only through digest-bearing tracked kinds inside the one theory. Its §7-item-3 half also misreads the plan — the store census there is not a dry run. What survives is one accurate bullet, and it is worth writing because it is the only place the move is ever paid.
rulings.fix: One bullet in PLAN.md §2, after the corrected cost bullet: the store-side cost falls only on function-package constants in WIP-keyed theories; where such a record predates the semantic change gate it takes SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §3 row 2 (forced CHANGED, no prefilter, no judge), so its cost is the constant plus the theory-internal dependents of the four tracked kinds that its mint enrols (theorem-alike dependents are re-interpreted once and never mint). No code change, no re-opened decision.

rulings.title: `f_dom` is an abbreviation, so the promised psimps edge does not exist
rulings.reason: I verified this directly rather than through the round-one citations. function_core.ML:575-576 builds the psimps premise as `HOLogic.mk_Trueprop (mk_acc domT R $ lhs)` with the source's own comment `(* "acc R lhs" *)`, and function_common.ML:126-132 defines mk_acc as `Const (\<^const_name>\<open>Wellfounded.accp\<close>, ...) $ R`; the `_dom` abbreviation is created only afterwards at function_core.ML:890-893. So no dependency edge can ever be named `..._dom`, and PLAN.md:116-117's assertion is unsatisfiable by any Const-level test — which is worse than a typo, because the one way to make it "pass" is to assert on the printed prop, i.e. through the printer, which Test_Sensitivity.thy:11-17 rule (a) is written against. The finding's THIRD bullet is refuted and must not be taken: ③ replaces the Defs axiom on BOTH paths, so the f_sumC edge is gone for psimps too; "claim the dead-edge removal only for the simps path" would put a false sentence into the accepted-gap register. Its stated mechanism is also wrong in a way worth not repeating — the psimps never contained `f_dom`; nothing "expanded it away".
rulings.fix: Two one-line edits, and leave PLAN.md:124-126 alone. (1) PLAN.md:100-101: replace "(and on `f_dom` when psimps are used)" with "(and, on the psimps path, on `Wellfounded.accp` and on the concealed, recordless `<f>_rel` — `_dom` is only the printed form of `accp <f>_rel`, function_core.ML:890-893)". (2) PLAN.md:116-117: replace "mentions `sens_pfun_dom`" with `mentions ... "Wellfounded.accp"` (it discriminates: today the sole prop is `sens_pfun == sens_pfun_sumC`, and accp cannot arrive through a `nat => nat` subject's type). Dropping that half of the bullet entirely is equally acceptable — the body-constant assertion on the same line already discriminates the psimps path.

rulings.title: The branch's theory safety rests on an unstated caller invariant
rulings.reason: Reduced to its one true residue, which is worth recording. ③ is the first digest source in this file whose answer can depend on WHICH theory env was built from: ② compares the axiom's theory with the constant's declaring theory (semantic_digest.ML:307-313, rationale :261-275), ⑤ uses the same filter, and class/locale content is frozen at declaration — while the registry lookup has no filter at all. S7 (Test_Sensitivity.thy:165-176) asserts env-independence as a design property, and Test_All.thy:46 builds env from main_thy over the whole cone, so an in-repo caller already sits where the precondition does not hold. Nothing goes wrong today, because production always builds env from the declaring theory (semantic_store.ML:1811 with theory_structure.ML:171-183). The finding's claim that the plan's own tests run in that unsound env is false — the new subjects are declared in the test theory itself (their visibility problem is tests-1, a different defect) — and its citation of Test_Sensitivity.thy:172 is backwards: that env is an ANCESTOR env whose purpose is to assert env-independence. Its fix overlaps with the overloading finding and is handled there.
rulings.fix: One sentence in PLAN.md §4's implementation notes and the same sentence in the comment block above `own_defining_axioms` that PLAN.md:102-104 already commits to writing: the registry is keyed by constant NAME only (Net drops the Const's type, net.ML:53-62) and the retrieved theorems carry no theory of their own (see def2-1), so this branch is sound only when env's theory is the constant's declaring theory — which every production caller guarantees (semantic_store.ML:1811 with theory_structure.ML:171-183).

rulings.title: Fabricated `c ^ ".simps"` prop names: unused and a false determinism rationale
rulings.reason: Two of three sub-claims survive. The rationale is false in its causal part: sem_constant keeps only `map snd axioms` (semantic_digest.ML:418-419), and within the new branch every prop carries one constant name, so the name component of the comparator is inert and the real order is raw Term_Ord.term_ord alone — the order §6 knowingly leaves latent. And the label is wrong for a mutual block: function.ML:65-70 notes `simps_by_f` under `derived_name fname "simps"` while the registry's `info.simps` is the whole block (:200-209), so digesting f would label g's clauses `f.simps`, a string that in the real theory denotes something strictly smaller. The "indistinguishable from the banned `.simps` fact lookup" sub-claim is REJECTED: what keeps the hack out is reading PLAN.md:88, which names the registry API; and the §5 primrec/definition control discriminates a fired branch anyway. The proposed replacement `Binding.name_of (#defname info)` is also rejected — it is unqualified (`f_g`) and morphism-dependent, while the function's other two branches return fully qualified names; one function whose output mixes long and short names is worse than one that is uniformly wrong in a documented way.
rulings.fix: Prose only. In PLAN.md §4 replace "name them `c ^ \".simps\"` / `c ^ \".psimps\"` so the existing sort ... is deterministic" with the accurate statement: the props are (name, term) pairs because the exported type demands it (semantic_digest.ML:65); nothing reads the name (:418-419); the branch shares the fallback's comparator, whose name component is constant here, so the order is Term_Ord.term_ord on the terms alone — with the residual sensitivity §6 records; and note that for a mutual block the label is not the name of any real fact. Keep the label itself.

rulings.title: `Proof_Context.init_global` per constant contradicts the file's per-pass env discipline
rulings.reason: The consistency point is real: env is where this file puts values derived once from thy (semantic_digest.ML:33-35, :75-82, :98-110), the repository's convention elsewhere is one context per bulk operation, and `Function_Common.retrieve_function_data : Proof.context -> ...` (function_common.ML:51) makes a context unavoidable, so the only question is where it is built. But the COST case is refuted and must not be used to justify it. The env comment's "quadratic" is explicit and about a different parameter (Theory.all_axioms_of looked up per constant, :73-74); Proof_Context.init_global is a bounded per-call constant (Datatab.map over the registered Proof_Data kinds, context.ML:612-614), the "2,191 constants" citation points at a timing line rather than a census, and the transfer-morphism paragraph argues for nothing at all — retrieve_function_data transfers whatever context it is handed, so hoisting removes zero transfers, and a non-function constant returns [] and pays nothing. Two lines either way, no behavioural difference, F7 covers it: the implementer may choose, and a re-review checks that the justification recorded is consistency, not performance.
rulings.fix: If taken: add `ctxt: Proof.context` to the env record (semantic_digest.ML:75-82) and set it in make_env (:98-110) as `Proof_Context.init_global thy` — the type is abstract in the signature so no client breaks — and rewrite PLAN.md:88 as `Function_Common.retrieve_function_data (#ctxt env) (Const (c, T))`, taking T from the Consts.the_constraint sem_constant has already computed at :414 rather than re-deriving it.

rulings.title: The new subjects are invisible to the `env` the suite's assertions use
rulings.reason: The mechanism is real and I confirmed it in the file: env is built at Test_Sensitivity.thy:20 from the theory value at that point, and the file documents the trap itself at :71-73 with the workaround at :75. A new subject declared after line 20 would make own_defining_axioms return [] both before and after the change, so acceptance item 1 would report FAIL-after on its first run. But "major/unmeetable" is wrong and is rejected: PLAN.md §5 specifies subjects and assertion content, not a line of ML, F7 delegates test spelling, the suite hands the implementer the idiom in a comment three lines from a working precedent, and acceptance item 1 is precisely the detector for this trap, so it cannot be made unmeetable by it. The finding's PREFERRED fix is rejected outright: hoisting the subjects above line 19 would break the file's one-subsection-per-concern layout AND silently change the input of the seven live assertions that read the file-level env — including making S2d/S2e measure a different world. One sentence costs nothing and saves a REPL round trip.
rulings.fix: One sentence in PLAN.md §5's first bullet: the new subsection declares its subjects immediately above its checks and builds its own env there (`Semantic_Digest.make_env \<^theory>`), exactly as S3 does at Test_Sensitivity.thy:74-78 — the file-level env at :20 predates them. Do NOT hoist the subjects above line 20.

rulings.title: The `instantiation … :: plus` subject does not make S2d discriminate the branch order
rulings.reason: I confirmed the decisive half myself: `grep -c '^instantiation\|^overloading' Groups.thy` returns 0, so Groups.plus_class.plus has no own-theory Defs axiom in any env (the nine measured ones are all downstream and dropped by same_theory, semantic_digest.ML:261-264, :307-313), ② is empty for it, and ③ — whose trigger is "② non-empty" — can never fire whatever the branch order. The proposed subject would not change that: its instance def is Test_Sensitivity-qualified and fails same_theory on both paths (the precedent is written out at :291-296). So the bullet would ship a subject that passes identically before and after, which is what Test_Sensitivity.thy:15-17 rule (b) forbids and what the parent plan warns is more dangerous than no test at all. The finding's placement half is also right but is tests-1's subject. Its rider about Function_Common's Item_Net being unmeasured is REJECTED: function.ML:215-217 feeds the same `fs` to add_function_data and to Spec_Rules.add, and VERIFICATION.md row 7 measured that exported term as `(+)`, so no new measurement is needed. The replacement subject it proposes (a new class + a local datatype + a `fun` instance) is also rejected as machinery bought against a non-risk: ① is the guard clause of own_defining_axioms and ② is computed only inside its else, so no implementation can put ③ ahead of ① without dismantling the function.
rulings.fix: Delete the fourth bullet of PLAN.md §5 (:119-121) and put one sentence in §6 in its place recording why the class-parameter case needs no runtime subject: the ①-before-③ order is enforced by shape (class_param_of is the guard clause of own_defining_axioms, semantic_digest.ML:387-389, and ② is computed only in its else), and for Groups.plus_class.plus ② is empty in every env because Groups.thy declares no instance at all. S2d/S2e stay exactly as they are, as no-regression checks.

rulings.title: No control discriminates the approved registry source from the Spec_Rules source VERIFICATION.md recommends
rulings.reason: The factual core is right and I re-checked both halves: add_function_data has exactly two writers in the distribution and the AFP (function.ML:136, :216), so partial_function is invisible to the registry, while partial_function.ML:304 does register an equational_recdef Spec_Rules item — so partial_function is the one behaviour where the approved source and the source VERIFICATION.md's closing paragraph recommends actually differ, and nothing in §5 pins it while primrec and definition, which F2 does not even mention, each get a control. That asymmetry is worth one word. But the "concrete failure" is rejected as inflated: it requires an implementer who ignores F3, F4, F5 and the verbatim API call at PLAN.md:88 in favour of a paragraph the verification document itself labels "for you to decide, not a decision". Tests pin the design that was chosen; they are not a guard against building a different one. The proposed assertion is also WRONG as written and must not be implemented: `option.fixp_fun` is an abbreviation inside locale partial_function_definitions (Partial_Function.thy:169 — I read it), so it can never occur in a certified term; and "exactly one prop" does not discriminate, since both candidate sources return one.
rulings.fix: Extend the control list at PLAN.md:117-118 from "a `primrec` and a `definition`" to "a `primrec`, a `definition`, and a `partial_function (option)`", asserting exactly what that line already asserts — the constant keeps exactly its Defs axiom (count and name). No new assertion shape and no hardcoded combinator name. Under the approved source this passes; under the rejected Spec_Rules source the prop's name changes and it fails. Optionally one sentence saying VERIFICATION.md's closing Recommendation paragraph is superseded by F3/F4/F5.

rulings.title: `fun`/`function` in a locale target never reaches the global registry
rulings.reason: Not a blocker, but the most important correction in the set. I verified every link: function.ML:135-136 and :215-216 install the registry entry with pervasive = false while Spec_Rules.add on the next line uses pervasive = true (spec_rules.ML:165); locale_declaration is `pervasive ? background_declaration ... #> locale_target_declaration ... #> standard_declaration (other <> 0)` (generic_target.ML:465-468), so with the flag false the background theory is fed only by apply_registrations, under a registration's morphism; and I read Bit_Operations.thy:1747-1760 — `function F` inside `locale fold2_bit_int`, whose only interpretations are at :1830-1836, i.e. no registration exists when the function is declared, and those later `global_interpretation ... defines` rewrite the key to and_int/or_int/xor_int. A bare-Const query cannot reach an application-keyed entry (net.ML:53-62). So fold2_bit_int.F, listed among the 20 record-eligible benefit constants, keeps its body-free Defs axiom and stays blind. The class case is different and must not be lumped in: a class IS globally registered at declaration (class_declaration.ML:341), so or_num (Bit_Operations.thy:3307-3310, inside `context linordered_euclidean_semiring_bit_operations`) is probably fine — VERIFICATION.md:412-419's measurement that the `_class.`-qualified sibling carries clean premise-free rules corroborates it. The finding's option (b) — feeding Spec_Rules back as a second source — is REJECTED: it reverses F3, forces F4, and re-imports the P6 unsoundness for a one-constant gain. So is any scan of Item_Net.content by head constant (same P6 failure mode through interpretations) and any recovery of a locale name from a constant's long name (a forbidden name-string hack).
rulings.fix: (1) One probe at implementation time, in the shape of the existing fun_probe: for each of the 40 function-package constants, evaluate `Function_Common.retrieve_function_data (Proof_Context.init_global thy) (Const (c, Consts.the_constraint (Sign.consts_of thy) c))` and record how many infos come back. Expect 0 for Bit_Operations.fold2_bit_int.F; confirm or_num comes back with its 9 clean simps (if it does not, the scope of the §6 bullet doubles). The same probe re-takes the census on the chosen source, which also picks up any unterminated `function` the Spec_Rules census could not see. (2) PLAN.md §2 last bullet: replace 40/34/20 with the registry-source figures and say the numbers are now measured through Function_Common.retrieve_function_data. (3) PLAN.md §6, new bullet: a `fun`/`function` in a LOCALE target reaches the global registry only through registrations of that locale and is then keyed on whatever the registration morphism yields, never on the bare locale constant — so it keeps its body-free Defs axiom and remains a limitation-#6 case; the shipped instance is Bit_Operations.fold2_bit_int.F. A CLASS target is not affected when the definition introduces no extra type variable. (4) Also correct PLAN.md:90-91: `Item_Net.retrieve` returns only entries keyed on a bare Const of the same name, not "all registrations".

rulings.title: Adding or deleting a `termination` proof moves the digest of unchanged equations
rulings.reason: Mechanism confirmed: the registry is keyed on the function TERM alone (`Item_Net.init (op aconv o apply2 fst) (single o fst)`, function_common.ML:261) and add_function_data uses Item_Net.update (:286), so the post-termination info with `simps = SOME simps` (function.ML:209-216) genuinely replaces the `simps = NONE` one, and ③ then reads different props on either side of one line. That is a new false-invalidation path worth one bullet. Three parts are refuted. There is no `f_dom` EDGE — the premise term is `accp <f>_rel` and `<f>_rel` is concealed, hence recordless — so the finding's amplification chain ("non-concealed abbrev, Kept, real store record") is void at its first link. "Walks every dependent" is unconditional where the gate makes it conditional on a CHANGED verdict. And the mirror case (`function` in A, `termination` in child B) is not a second defect but the stability the finding is asking for: A's digest keeps the psimps form permanently, and since the psimps carry the same equation bodies, equation edits are still caught — refusing to let a child theory rewrite a parent constant's digest is the deliberate same-theory discipline.
rulings.fix: One bullet in PLAN.md §6: which of simps/psimps the registry holds is decided by the `termination` proof (function.ML:205-216 re-registers via Item_Net.update), so adding or deleting that proof moves the digest of a function whose equations never changed — one re-interpretation plus one judge call, dependents walled by an UNCHANGED verdict. Symmetrically, a `termination` proved in another theory never reaches the declaring theory's env, so such a constant keeps the psimps form; no equation change is missed either way. Fold def1-4's diamond clause into the same bullet.

rulings.title: Proposal: take the registry's `input_eqns` instead of `simps`/`psimps`
rulings.reason: Refuted by its own stated decision criterion, and I checked the sources rather than relying on the rebuttals. input_eqns is built from the props of `prep fixspec eqns lthy` (function.ML:70-81), which are checked in a context where the function names are plain fixes, and the package REQUIRES that head to be a Free — split_def does `fst (dest_Free head)` and check_defs errors "Illegal equation head" otherwise (function_common.ML:137-168). No morphism on the path can turn a Free into a Const: Variable.export_morphism's term action is Term_Subst.generalize, which maps Free to Var at most. The finding's cited counter-evidence (`fs` printing as a constant) proves nothing — `fs` are the terms Local_Theory.define returns, never Frees being converted. The consequence in this codebase is fatal: normalize renames every Free positionally (semantic_digest.ML:151-157) and deps_of_term collects only Consts (:237, :243-252), so a constant's own equations would mention neither it nor its mutual partners, and the f->g edge of `fun f and g` that PLAN.md:92-94 relies on would vanish — the same mechanism the proposal sells as benefit (iii) working against it. It would also record unchecked user input as a constant's meaning (for an unterminated `function`, an equation that is literally false without its domain premise), and it rests on a field with zero consumers anywhere in the distribution or the AFP, absent from Isabelle2024's info record, in a repository that ships both distributions. Do not put it to the user.

rulings.title: §6 records the wrong expectation for Nominal: `nominal_function` is body-free in Defs AND invisible to the chosen registry
rulings.reason: I verified both halves in the AFP snapshot this repository ships. nominal_function_core.ML:1021 defines the function through `define_function (defname ^ "_sumC_def") ...`, i.e. its Defs axiom is body-free exactly like `fun`'s — so it is a blind spot TODAY, not an unmeasured "expected to carry a body". And it keeps its own registry: nominal_function_common.ML:110 is a separate `add_function_data` over a separate NominalFunctionData item net, so Function_Common.retrieve_function_data returns nothing for it and ③ can never fire. This is a genuine consequence of F3 that the plan's own §6 mis-states, and it is checkable by reading, not a hypothetical. It also sharpens what F3 costs relative to the source that was actually measured, since nominal_termination.ML:69 is one of the five equational_recdef producers VERIFICATION.md:56 lists. No instance in this heap; this is a register correction, not a code change.
rulings.fix: PLAN.md §6: (a) delete "Nominal" from the "Commands not measured (expected to carry a body in Defs)" bullet at :144-147 — the expectation is false and checkable; (b) add a bullet naming the class rather than the instance: a definitional package that produces a body-free `_sumC` Defs axiom but writes its OWN registry instead of Function_Common's is not reached by ③ and remains a blind spot; the shipped instance is Nominal2's nominal_function/nominal_termination (nominal_function_core.ML:1021, nominal_function_common.ML:110). Keep old_recdef, partial_function and partial_function_mr out of that bullet — they carry their body in Defs and lose nothing.

rulings.title: The outcome is filed under the wrong limitation entry (#6 is about dead edges)
rulings.reason: The distinction is correct and worth making: #6's subject is an edge whose TARGET holds no record, while the defect this plan fixes — and the shapes that survive it (same-theory `overloading`, `fun` inside `instantiation`, `fun` in a locale target) — is a Kept, record-holding constant whose OWN definitional content never enters its OWN digest. Filing the survivors under a heading rated "low" with no row of their own in the index table would hide them from the next reader looking for exactly that question. But whether to open a new numbered entry or extend #6 is a documentation-structure call inside a register the implementer maintains, and F7 covers plan and documentation details; either shape can be made honest. A re-review should check that the surviving shapes are findable under a heading that names them, wherever they end up.
rulings.fix: Implementer's choice. Either add a new entry to doc/invalidation_limitations.md (with its own row in the index table at :19-31) named for the class — a constant whose own definitional content does not reach its own digest — listing the surviving shapes, and leave in #6 only the true sentence PLAN.md:124-126 wants there; or extend #6 with an explicitly separated subsection. PLAN.md:124-126 then names whichever place was chosen.

rulings.title: §5 updates the acceptance table but not CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md §7.3 item 1
rulings.reason: Confirmed by reading the register: archive/plans/CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md §7.3 is headed "最容易被误删、实则不可替代（历经实测的四条）" and its item 1 is a complete description of own_defining_axioms' three layers, including the measured evidence for each. ③ inserts a fourth layer into the middle of exactly that function, and its reason (the Defs axiom is `f ≡ f_sumC`, so the equations exist only in the package's registry) is invisible from the code — which is the precise failure mode §7.3 exists to prevent. PLAN.md §5 lists the documentation touch points and names §14 and the limitation register but not §7.3, so after implementation the module's own "do not delete this" register would describe a function that no longer exists. Mechanical, one line.
rulings.fix: Add one line to PLAN.md §5's documentation list: archive/plans/CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md §7.3 item 1 gains the registry branch, with the two facts that make it undeletable — the function package's Defs axiom carries no body (`f ≡ f_sumC`), so the equations are reachable only through Function_Common.retrieve_function_data; and it must REPLACE rather than ADD, or a constant with both would be counted twice. Edit it by hand (no scripted edits to plan documents).

rulings.title: `Item_Net.merge` collapses two registrations of the same function by term alone
rulings.reason: Verified: the net's equality is `op aconv o apply2 fst` (function_common.ML:261) — the registered TERM only, not the info — and merge is `fold_rev (fn y => if member items1 y then I else cons y) (content items2) items1` (item_net.ML:67-70) with member using that same equality. So in a diamond where one parent proved `termination` and the other did not, the second parent's differing info is silently discarded and ③ reads simps or psimps depending on parent order. Production is not exposed (env is always the declaring theory) but the exported own_defining_axioms and the Main-wide env of Test_All.thy:46 are. No instance in this heap. It answers the brief's determinism question precisely: the plan's sort makes the prop ORDER deterministic, not the registry CONTENT. One clause, no code.
rulings.fix: Fold one clause into the §6 bullet that the termination finding already asks for: the registry keeps one info per function TERM, so in a diamond import a descendant env's answer depends on parent order when one parent proved `termination` and the other did not.

rulings.title: The exported signature comment of `own_defining_axioms` becomes false and is not on the fix list
rulings.reason: Correct, and it is the comment the consumers actually read. semantic_digest.ML:63-65 states the contract as "The defining axioms retained for a constant after the own-theory filter", and on every path today the first component is a real axiom or fact name (:382, :393-395). After ③ neither half holds: the props are derived theorems that never passed the own-theory filter (the filter gates whether the branch fires, not which registry entries it consumes) and the name is fabricated. PLAN.md:102-104 promises to correct the file header and the comment block above the function but not this one, and the sensitivity suite is an API reader of exactly this contract (Test_Sensitivity.thy:55, :58, :60). This subsumes def2-3, which says the same thing; I count them once. The project's terminology rule makes it binding rather than cosmetic: leaving the old word covering the new thing is the drift that rule forbids.
rulings.fix: Add semantic_digest.ML:63-65 to the list PLAN.md:102-104 commits to correcting, and restate the contract: the propositions that carry a constant's own definitional content after the own-theory filter — its own-theory Defs axioms, or, for a function-package constant, its equations from the package's registry, which replace that axiom — with the first component a fact-like label that is not necessarily the name of any fact.

rulings.title: The registry answer carries no theory attribution at all; the type is the only discriminator it offers
rulings.reason: The first half is a genuine and load-bearing insight that nobody else stated, and it DEFENDS a user decision instead of attacking one, which is why it is worth writing down once: retrieve_function_data maps `transform_function_data (Morphism.transfer_morphism' ctxt)` over the answer (function_common.ML:279-281), Morphism.fact begins with `map (join_transfer ...)` (morphism.ML:149, :219), Thm.join_transfer replaces the certificate with the join (thm.ML:674) and Thm.theory_name reads exactly that certificate — so every returned simp reports the ENV's theory, and the rest of the info record (`fs`, a bare `defname`) carries none either. The "② non-empty" proxy of F4 is therefore not laziness; it is the only theory evidence in reach, and any future proposal to "read the theory off the info" is impossible, not merely inelegant. The second half — the correct spelling of the type test, and why typ_instance-both-ways, Consts.type_scheme and import_function_data are each worse — belongs to the proposal and is handled under the overloading finding.
rulings.fix: Record the first half in PLAN.md §4's implementation notes and in the comment block above own_defining_axioms (merge with the elegance-2 sentence): the registry answer is re-stamped with the env's theory by the transfer morphism, so it carries no theory of its own; "② non-empty" is the only theory evidence available, which is why F4's criterion is the right one and not a shortcut.

rulings.title: (② non-empty, registration at the declared type) is a theorem, not two heuristics
rulings.reason: This is the strongest argument in the whole set and it is the reason I route the type guard to the user rather than dismissing it. I verified its load-bearing citation: Defs.update_specs calls disjoint_specs, which errors "Clash of specifications" whenever two specifications of one constant have non-disjoint argument types (defs.ML:162-168, :177-178). A specification at the constant's DECLARED type overlaps every other, so it cannot coexist with a second one. Hence if ② is non-empty and some registration is at the declared type, that registration IS the definition behind ②'s single axiom — the pair is closed, not two stacked heuristics, and `length from_defs = 1` becomes a derived fact rather than a condition (which is precisely why the count guard is the wrong instrument). It also excludes the downstream-contamination case, since a descendant defining the constant at its full general type would clash with the own-theory one. Under the instruction to weigh elegance as heavily as correctness, this is the shape that makes the invariant impossible to violate instead of asking people to remember it. It is a proposal and not a fix for two reasons: it narrows the rule the user approved, and the type comparison is unmeasured for an ordinary polymorphic `fun` (the registered type and Consts.the_constraint reach their schematic form by different routes, and class operations are declared with strip_sortsT then given a sorted constraint, class.ML:402-407), and this plan's charter does not accept unmeasured filters.
rulings.fix: See the proposals list. If adopted: one conjunct in ③ (Theory.check_overloading's own one-direction test, theory.ML:301-315), PLAN.md:89-91 rewritten so the type-blindness of Item_Net.retrieve reads as the hazard it is rather than as a feature, PLAN.md:47-50's reliance on where the `consts` declaration sits deleted, and two free acceptance checks in §7 item 1 — the census must come back at the same count, and or_num must still be in it.

rulings.title: The new branch would be the third inline sort comparator in one function
rulings.reason: Small and correct: after ③ the function carries three orderings (name-only at :396, name-then-term at :383-384, and a third written out again for the new branch), and the project's reuse rule says refactor rather than copy-paste-and-modify. Binding the comparator once above spec_rule_axioms and using it in both places is two lines and leaves the Defs branch's name-only sort untouched (changing that would move digests outside the function-package family). I route it to the implementer rather than mandating it because it is a pure code-shape call inside the section F7 delegates, and because its accompanying prose corrections are already mandated under elegance-3 and the sort finding. A re-review checks that the fallback and the new branch share one comparator if the refactor is taken, and that nothing outside the function-package family moved either way.
rulings.fix: If taken: bind `fun prop_ord ((a, s), (b, t)) = (case string_ord (a, b) of EQUAL => Term_Ord.term_ord (s, t) | ord => ord)` above spec_rule_axioms, use it at :383-384 and in the new branch, and leave :396 alone.

proposals_for_user: F6 must be re-put, because it was decided on a false sentence. §6 says the raw-term sort is "unreachable from one `fun` (two clauses of one `fun` cannot be alpha-variants of each other)". That is not the condition. `Term_Ord.term_ord` settles a tie by the schematic variable's index and then its NAME (term_ord.ML:127, reached through hd_ord at :157-158) whenever the first position at which two props separate is a variable position — and those two fields are exactly what `normalize` exists to erase. I walked a two-clause example by hand: for `fun h where "h x True = x" | "h y False = y"` the comparison reaches the ?x/?y pair BEFORE it reaches True/False, so renaming `x` to `z` reverses the sorted prop list and moves the digest for a cosmetic edit. It is also no longer a corner case after this change: today the raw-term comparison only breaks ties inside the `axiomatization` fallback, because the Defs branch sorts by axiom name alone; with every prop of the new branch carrying the same fabricated name it becomes the sole ordering for every multi-clause `fun`. Nothing goes stale — the error direction is a false positive costing one re-interpretation plus one judge call, and 0 of this heap's 40 function-package constants are exposed. So the decision may well stand; it should just stand on the true fact. If you do want it closed, the change is confined to the new branch and must order by a normalised KEY rather than replace the returned props, since those props are what the sensitivity suite asserts on.

Whether to give rule ③ a type guard, or to record the gap in §6 instead. As approved, ③'s entire guard is the proxy "② is non-empty", and what it then consumes comes from a lookup with no filter at all: Isabelle's term net encodes `Const (c, _)` as `AtomK c` with the type thrown away (net.ML:53-62), so the `T = Consts.the_constraint` of PLAN.md:88-89 does nothing and every registration under that name comes back. The plan's stated protection (PLAN.md:47-50, "the `overloading` construction leaves from_defs empty") is an accident of where probe P6 put the `consts` declaration, not a property of `overloading`. The shape it misses is shipped in the AFP this repository carries: Amortized_Complexity/Pairing_Heap_List2_Analysis.thy:22-38 declares `consts sz :: "'a => nat"` and, in ONE overloading block in that same theory, defines it by `fun size_hps` and by two `definition`s. All three Defs axioms pass same_theory, ③ fires, and the two definition bodies leave sz's digest permanently — a new blind spot of exactly the class this project exists to remove. Zero instances in the 88-theory heap, so nothing changes today. Two ways out: (a) record the shape in §6 as a surviving limitation and ship ③ as approved — cheapest, no code; (b) add one conjunct, keeping only registrations at the constant's own declared type, spelled the way Isabelle already spells this test in `Theory.check_overloading` (theory.ML:301-315): `Sign.typ_instance thy (Consts.the_constraint (Sign.consts_of thy) c, Logic.varifyT_global T_reg)`, one direction only. Option (b) is the more elegant by a real margin, and not merely by one more check: `Defs` itself refuses a second specification whose argument types overlap the first (defs.ML:162-168), and a specification at the declared type overlaps every other — so "② non-empty AND a registration at the declared type" entails that the registration is this constant's own definition. The invariant then holds by construction instead of by argument, and the same conjunct also closes the downstream-contamination case. It costs one probe first: the comparison is unmeasured for an ordinary polymorphic `fun`, and for class operations the declared type and the stored constraint are known to differ on sorts, so the acceptance run must confirm the census does not shrink and that `or_num` is still in it.

Keep the store-copy permission of §7 item 3, but it cannot answer the cost question as worded. The semantic digest and the dependency list are computed ONLY for WIP theories — semantic_store.ML:1804-1808 hands every entry of a persistent theory NONE and [] without ever calling Semantic_Digest.semantics_of, and that function has exactly two production call sites, both inside the WIP branch. Every one of the 20 "record-eligible" constants sits in a loaded HOL theory, i.e. persistent, so the ML change is unreachable for them and their price is zero; the 40/34/20 figures are a reach census, not a cost. The permission is still needed, because the other half of item 3 — the dry run of Sim_Measure_A1 — has a WIP-keyed subject and is the only end-to-end check the plan has. Only the clause "the count of record-holding function-package constants in the store (the one-time cost)" should change, to count function-package constants holding a WIP-keyed record. One caveat worth knowing before you grant it: a fresh copy of the production store may not contain Sim_Measure_A1's records at all, in which case `narquil` would count as a seed merely by being uncached and would prove nothing.
